articleTitle: Palladium Films as Electrodes on Carbyne-Based Devices
abstract: Palladium contacts were deposited on a carbyne-enriched nanocoating, and the sheet resistance of the carbyne material was measured before and after the deposition of different thicknesses of the electrode films, to explore if there is unwanted interaction between the materials in contact. It was deduced diffusion of palladium particles into the carbyne, and it was found that it is thickness dependent. It was found that ~200 nm Pd films caused variation of the carbyne film’s sheet resistance from 130 to 118 kΩ/sq and 400 nm Pd resulted in a 27.9 kΩ/sq of the carbyne, which requires an additional blocking layer to prevent the diffusion process. Nickel thin film proved to be an effective barrier to resolving this issue. Studying contacts between a variety of metals and carbyne film is of great importance for the fabrication of future organic chip devices.

articleTitle: Spray Deposition of Conjugated Polymer/Graphene Ink as an Electrode in Future Chemical Biosensing Devices
abstract: In this study, a solution of conjugated polymer PEDOT:PSS ink mixed with graphene was spray deposited on a flexible substrate at different deposition conditions. The film thickness, sheet resistance, surface roughness and transparency were measured for the samples produced at different temperatures of spraying and a different number of spraying cycles. The most favorable conditions for obtaining uniform, low resistive, and highly transparent film in a repeatable manner were determined. At a substrate temperature of 100 °C, the sheet resistance was 56.6 Ω/sq, the surface roughness was 5.95 nm and the average transparency in the visible range of wavelength was 91 %. The coating is intended for electrodes in a sweat sensor, which will be interfaced with transition metal chalcogenides and MXenes in different sensing architectures that can be electrical, or optical. As such, the obtained results for the PEDOT:PSS/graphene coatings are according to the state-of-the-art of the conventional metal-oxide transparent films. The parameters are satisfactory and the organic electrode can be incorporated into a device structure.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of YOLO Models for Automatic Crop and Weed Detection
abstract: Accurate weed mapping is essential for the implementation of weed management in order to maintain high crop yields and less chemical pollution. This paper focuses on the performance evaluation of YOLO models for automatic crop and weed detection. The research aims to develop weed detection models using one-stage deep learning-based object detectors by transferring pre-trained object detection models to a selected weed dataset. The models are trained on annotated images from a public dataset and evaluated based on detection accuracy. Results demonstrate promising training performance, with approximately 70% mean average precision achieved in 100 training epochs. YOLOv5x exhibits the best performance among the studied models, achieving the highest precision, recall, and mean average precision (0.72, 0.75, and 0.74, respectively). The findings indicate that models with deeper or larger backbone networks tend to provide higher detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Adsorption-Based Micro/Nanosensors for Protein Detection: Influence of Protein Conformation Changes and Analyte Depletion on the Sensor Response
abstract: Proper modeling of biosensor time response should include all processes relevant for sensor signal generation. This is essential for reliable interpretation of measurement results, which affects conclusions on the presence and amount of biological agents in an analyzed sample, and also conclusions on the analyzed characteristics of biomolecular interactions. In this paper we present a model of time response of adsorption-based protein micro/nanosensors, which besides the reversible adsorption of analyte molecules includes depletion of the sample due to adsorption of molecules on the sensing surface, as well as the conformation change of the adsorbed molecules. We then use a model for the analysis of the separate influence of each of these processes on the response, as well as their joint effect. The results show that neglecting any of the two mentioned processes may lead to an erroneous interpretation of measurement results. Therefore the presented sensor response model is of importance for the improvement of accuracy of biomolecular detection and quantification.

articleTitle: Voltage Glitch Filter and Detector with Self-Checking Capability for FPGA Implementation
abstract: Short voltage pulses (glitches) in digital circuits resulting from high energy particle strikes or electromagnetic noise may cause data loss and system failure. Therefore, glitch filtering is essential to ensure the system’s reliability. In addition, detecting and recording the occurrence of voltage glitches allows for self-awareness of the system, which is important in applications where dynamic fault tolerance is required. This paper presents a design of a digital circuit for filtering and detecting transient glitches in FPGA-based systems. The proposed solution is based on the standard glitch filter with delay line and guard gate realized with NAND gates, and two binary counters for counting the number of glitches. To enable the detection of transient and permanent faults in the counters, duplication with comparison is applied. Preliminary FPGA evaluation is presented.

articleTitle: Prediction of Generated Single Event Transient Pulse Width Using Artificial Intelligence Methods
abstract: In this work, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms for the prediction of generated Single Event Transient (SET) pulse width in standard combinational cells is analyzed. The SET generation is characterized using the current injection approach in Spectre simulations. Based on conducted simulations, the dataset of SET pulse width in terms of gate driving strength, supply voltage, temperature and particle Linear Energy Transfer (LET) is created. The dataset is then used to train six standard machine learning models: linear regression, polynomial regression, support vector machine, decision tree, random forest, and multi-layer perceptron. For all models, the largest prediction error was observed for small SET pulse widths (< 100 ps). The multilayer perceptron model has shown the best accuracy in SET pulse width prediction, with the correlation coefficient R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> > 0.99.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Electric Breakdowns in Metal-Insulator-Silicon Capacitor Structures with HfO2/Al2O3 Layers for Non-Volatile Memory Applications
abstract: The electric breakdown of memory capacitors with atomic layer deposited HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanolaminated stacks was investigated by voltage ramp method and constant voltage stress. Two types of capacitors – with 2.4 and 3.5 nm tunnel SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer were investigated, before and after O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> annealing. Breakdown voltages ~ - 30 V were obtained independently of the thickness of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> annealing seems to increase the charge to breakdown due to higher current through the capacitors. The effect is more pronounced for structures with 3.5 nm tunnel layer. The results indicate that the electric breakdown is mainly determined by Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> blocking layer and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanolaminate. The electric breakdown is accompanied by positive charge build-up and generation of interface states at SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si interface. The latter process is subdued in the annealed samples.

articleTitle: Design of an Energy-Efficient SRAM Cell with Optimum Cell Ratio
abstract: The pre-charge, write enables, sense amplifier enables, read enables, and rows and columns encoders of SRAM cell are all considered in this paper. In SRAM memory cell, these components play different roles and are usually implemented as separate circuit blocks around the SRAM memory array. The 8T SRAM cell was built using the Tanner Tool on 45nm technology, which is an industry-standard tool. This tool helps in designing and simulating integrated circuits, including SRAM cells. To establish an efficient SRAM architecture, several semiconductor circuits are available. SRAM cells commonly use a four-transistor circuit in low-power VLSI applications. The 4T SRAM cell is a widely used design due to its balance between performance, area efficiency, and power consumption. To boost power efficiency at various ideal cell ratios, 8 transistors (8T) SRAM designs are employed instead of conventional circuits in this analysis. While designing an 8T SRAM circuitry incorporating write driver logics, power consumption is assessed including both static and dynamic conditions. This research involves the investigation of variable decay of power, which refers to the dynamic power consumption that varies based on the circuit activity and input patterns. Analysing and characterizing the dynamic power behaviour of SRAM cells under different operating conditions and workloads will be an important aspect of my research. Tanner's EDA tool suite is deployed for schematic entry and capture of the SRM cell. T-Spice based simulation is used to obtain the netlist, whereas, W- Edit is run to review the waveforms. The assessment of circuitry is carried out at the voltage of 1.1V. The purpose of this research is to create a design and compute all of the characteristics that contribute to the stability of an 8T Static RAM cell in 45nm technology, as well as the optimum cell ratio based on the measured parameters i.e. read noise margin (RSNM), hold noise margin (HSNM), read delay, and write delay.

articleTitle: Investigation of Annealing Temperature and Gamma Irradiation on HfO2/Dy2O3/Al2O3/n-Si (100) Memory Capacitor
abstract: The effect of annealing temperature and gamma irradiation on Al/HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Dy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/n-Si (100) tri-layer capacitors have been studied intensively. The HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Dy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> were fabricated by using both RF magnetron sputtering and E-beam evaporation techniques, respectively. The samples were annealed at 300<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C, 500<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C,700<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C, and 900<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C in N2 ambient for 40min. The device annealed at 700<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C had a large memory window of 8.22V under sweeping voltage ±12V compared to other annealed devices. This is attributed to the excellent charge storage capability of the device. Thereafter, this device was exposed to gamma irradiation at various doses of 4 Gy to 16 Gy. C-V and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>/ɷ-V measurements were performed before and after irradiation at 1MHz. The C-V curves shifted toward the positive voltage side. This could be related to the oxide-trapped and interface-trapped charges generated during irradiation

articleTitle: MXene Nanostrip Plasmonic Metamaterials for Mechanical Sensing and Enhanced Optical Absorption
abstract: Nanocomposites are among the most prominent subjects of material science and enable an enormous number of applications in diverse areas. They are of immense importance for micro and nanoelectronics, sensorics and photonics. They allow one to embed, tailor and program not only the fundamental material properties (a typical example being different metamaterials with traits usually not met in nature) but also to impart multifunctionalities to them. Here we consider a plasmonic metamaterial nanocomposite built of MXene strips suspended in a dielectric host. We numerically analyzed the influence of nanostrip orientation and ordering on the metamaterial properties. We utilized finite element method (FEM) for our electromagnetic simulations. We enhanced our stochastic nanocomposite metamaterial structure by adding a conductive backplate to further increase its optical absorption. The proposed multifunctional MXene-based metametamaterials can be used as a basis for refractometric sensors of any physical quantity that can modify nanostrips orientation, including mechanical sensing. Combining traditional and novel plasmonic approach to optical absorbers structure allows for a relatively simple "bottom up" approach to broadband optical superabsorber design.

articleTitle: Thick Resistive Film Application on Steel Bars for Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: This paper aims to examine the applicability of thick-film piezo-resistive sensors on steel bars for the structural health monitoring purposes. A thick film ceramic piezo-resistive sensor was manufactured and used to investigate the possibility of its application on a bar. To form the device, Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ru<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> resistive thick-film composition was used in combination with Pd/Ag conductive composition on alumina ceramic substrates. Six conductive pads divided the resistor into seven identical segments. Sensor was subjected to a three-point bending test. After it was glued to a steel bar like a common foil strain gauge, a four-point bending test was performed on a sensor placed on the upper side of the bar. Under strain, sensor experienced reversible deformation that was registered as a change in the resistivity of the film. Evaluation of the sensor included measurements of the resistance change under the applied strain, determination of the gage factor and investigations of its physical integrity and temperature stability.

articleTitle: Robustness Validation of a mm-Wave Model based on GRU Neural Networks for a GaN Power HEMT
abstract: Recently a GaN HEMT small-signal model based on gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural networks has been proposed and it has been proved that a very good accuracy can be achieved by using the developed modeling approach. However, as the GRU networks are recurrent networks, meaning that the previous states contribute to the current output, the aim of the work is to test and validate the behavior of the GaN HEMT model depending on the input order and history in order to derive the corresponding outcomes and to gain a better understanding of the inherent features of the developed modeling strategy.

articleTitle: Electrical Characteristics and Reliability Analysis of Hetero-dielectric Dual Tunnel Diode TFET
abstract: This paper presents a hetero-dielectric dual tunnel diode (HD-DTD) TFET formed by p++ type highly doped L-shaped trench with hetero gate dielectric and its electrical parameters are compared with conventional C-SOI TFET structure. Conventional SOI devices have kink effect. Kink effect is mitigated by eliminating the accumulation of holes by the tunnel current of the DTD. The reliability issues have been examined by considering gaussian type traps. Different electrical parameters have been quantified against interface trap types (donor or acceptor) and trap concentration. Moreover, flicker noise behavior of the proposed TFET design has been studied. The dependency of noise spectral density on frequency has been explored. Without considering interface trap, the device provides ION/IOFF ratio of 5.35 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> and SS of 17 mV/decade.

articleTitle: ChatGPT in IoT Systems: Arduino Case Studies
abstract: Since the beginning of this year, the novel large language model (LLM) based ChatGPT conversational agent has been in spotlight, due to its comprehensiveness across many fields – from novel writing to playing board games. In this paper, it is explored how it can be leveraged within IoT systems, taking into account both the novel scenarios enabled relying on ChatGPT’s power of question answering and software development as well. As example, two case studies related to Arduino platform are considered: 1) ChatGPT-based predictions on sensor data collected by Arduino 2) model-driven automated Arduino code generation.

articleTitle: The 4 Watt UHF VDMOS Power Amplifier for Space Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimental investigation results of the UHF power amplifier (PA) based on a silicon MOSFET manufactured by vertical diffusion technology (VDMOS). The designed PA has operating frequency range from 800 to 1100 MHz, power gain 10 dB and maximal PAE 36 %. Single-event effects (SEEs) and total ionizing dose (TID) test results are presented for VDMOS transistors in this study.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Bee Hive Monitoring System
abstract: Beehive monitoring can provide useful information for people associated with beekeeping to help to manage their honey bee (Apis mellifera) colonie. This paper presents the development and experimental results of a IoT enabled bee hive monitoring system

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Monic-Chebyshev Polynomials for Microwave Filters Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to microwave lowpass filters designing that meet some challenges of modern systems in terms of size, performance and cost. By utilizing the monic Chebyshev polynomials as a filter characteristic function, the proposed design achieves minimum passband insertion loss and maximum cutoff slope. Using the Matlab software, steady-state responses are plotted over a wide frequency range to elucidate the proposed design.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Serial NPN Power Transistor in a Negative Voltage Regulator Operating in Various X-Ray Environments
abstract: Negative low-dropout voltage regulator was examined in two various bremsstrahlung X-ray fields. The principal values used to estimate the radiation response of the circuit were variations of the serial power transistor dropout voltage and its base current. In a similar manner as in the previous research, done on low-dropout voltage regulators with lateral PNP power transistors, an effort was made to utilize a method for indirect experimental characterization of the serial transistor’s base current. However, due to the distinction of circuit topology implemented in the negative voltage regulator examined, there were limitations for indirect calculation of the base current of the serial transistor. The main reason for this is the implementation of a coupling diode, connected between the output terminal of the voltage regulator and the collector contact of the driver transistor. The use of a detailed SPICE simulation model made it possible to determine the bias conditions required for the successful implementation of the specified method.

articleTitle: Physics-Driven Methods for Adaptive Optics Effect in Extended Reality: Eliminating the Need for Corrective Lenses
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) as a broad category encompassing virtual reality (VR), mixed reality (MR), and augmented reality (AR) technology, faces a notable default-practice constraint: the requirement for the users to be without vision problems or wear corrective contact lenses. Several users are unable to use contact lenses due to discomfort, allergies, dryness, or post-refractive surgery limitations. This paper delves into physics-driven methods to address this conflict, focusing specifically on the innovative integration of adaptive optics. Drawing inspiration from past research and current technological advancements, we project into the future of XR, envisioning a landscape where the amalgamation of adaptive optics, eye-tracking, and light field displays provides an immersive experience without the constraints of traditional visual corrective aids.

articleTitle: A Hardware Generator of Two-Dimensional Cell- Averaging Constant False Alarm Rate Processors
abstract: Two-dimensional constant false alarm rate (2D-CFAR) procedure is an indispensable part of radar signal processing for object detection in cluttered and noisy environments. A software implementation of this adaptive algorithm cannot achieve real-time data processing performance for many radar applications due to its computationally intensive nature. Besides the processing speed, another important feature of these detectors is their ability to adjust to different environments and weather conditions. Therefore, a parametrizable hardware design code generator of two-dimensional cell-averaging CFAR (2D-CA-CFAR) detectors with fully streaming input and output interfaces and a novel pipeline architecture that exploits a high level of parallelism is captured inside the Chisel hardware description language. The proposed hardware generator is designed in a modular fashion. It supports dynamic configuration options that include reference and guard window sizes, the radar data matrix (RDM) dimensions, as well as compile-time parameters such as input and output data types and widths and stream-out interface configuration. A range of representative 2D-CA-CFAR instances are implemented and mutually compared on a commercially available FPGA platform.

articleTitle: Design of a Ternary Fredkin Reversible Gate
abstract: Several realizations of a reversible ternary Fredkin gate are developed based on Muthukrishnan-Stroud controlled-controlled Sum modulo 3 gates and controlled scaling gates. It is shown that under positive polarity, the proposed Fredkin gates have the expected controlled swap behaviour and that under mixed polarity, other behaviours are possible. Most introduced realizations have a lower realization complexity than realizations found in the literature.

articleTitle: Utilisation of Raspberry Pi 4 and RP2040 microcontroller for PID measurement and control
abstract: In this article, the design of a high precision, low-cost PID acquisition system and the design of PID control system are shown. The PID acquisition system consists of a measurement unit connected to a Raspberry Pi 4, where temperature data is stored and plotted. The Ziegler–Nichols tuning method is used to calculate and tune the PID control system. The PID control system is based on a dual-core microcontroller Raspberry Pi Pico RP2040 using a standard closed-loop PID algorithm. The systems run using Python and MicroPython. This article uses PTC heating element temperature control as an example.

articleTitle: Prediction of Pollen Levels Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This study explores the use of machine learning techniques for the prediction of pollen levels. The aim of the research is to develop an accurate model that can forecast pollen levels and help individuals with allergies to manage their symptoms. The study utilizes data from various sources, including pollen counts and applies machine learning algorithms. The results indicate that these techniques can provide accurate predictions of pollen levels, which can be used to support individuals with allergies and inform public health policies.

articleTitle: A System for Detection and Tracking of Oculo-Vestibular Complications Associated with Extended Reality Headset Usage
abstract: The rising popularity of extended reality (XR) technology has brought about significant transformations in diverse fields such as gaming, entertainment, and education. However, along with the prolonged and frequent usage of other digital devices, the use of XR headsets has raised concerns among healthcare providers due to potential health complications. This paper aims to examine the various health issues associated with XR headset usage and introduces a novel system for detecting and monitoring XR-related ocular and vestibular complications, followed by guidance and actions for preventing further complications. The system leverages the GPT-4 model to generate adaptive health check questions, providing individualized monitoring for each user. It utilizes a Raspberry Pi equipped with a camera to collect and analyze user data in real-time, focusing on balance-related complications. This system's objective is to enable early detection and prevention of these issues, thereby improving the safety and overall user experience of XR technologies.

articleTitle: Characterization of Humidity Sensor Based on Nanostructured Porous LNTO Ceramics
abstract: The present paper reports on the room-temperature characteristics of the impedance-type humidity sensor based on nanostructured porous lithium-niobium-titanium-oxide (LNTO) ceramics modified with 2 wt% of ZnO as functional additive. These ceramics were prepared by using a solid–state reaction method and final cylindrical pellet samples were sintered at 900°C for 4 h. Using scanning electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction techniques, structural analysis confirmed the desired porous nature of the synthesized LNTO ceramics with an average crystallite size in the nano range. Within a wide relative humidity range from 15% to 85%, the LNTO-based ceramic sensor exhibits a linear response with an impedance change of about two orders of magnitude at the optimal operating frequency of 15 kHz. Furthermore, fast response (17 s) and recovery (28 s), relatively small hysteresis (3.5%), repeatability and good long-term stability were also obtained.

articleTitle: Using TCAD Simulations to Verify the McWhorter Method for Assessing Trapped Charge in Dielectric
abstract: This study arises from the difficulty of obtaining comprehensive proprietary information from MOSFET manufacturers, which may have influenced the method's precision. To mitigate this, an irradiation experiment was conducted to estimate typical trapped charge densities. Subsequently, a MOSFET structure with thick oxide resembling experimental conditions was simulated. The McWhorter method was used with the channel doping parameter adjusted by a factor of 10 from the correct value in TCAD simulations. Notably, the smallest deviations were observed when the density of fixed traps (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ft</inf>) exceeded that of switching traps (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</inf>), reflecting a more realistic scenario for irradiated devices. The research explores potential future directions, including defining energy levels for switching traps, experimental procedures with varying oxide thicknesses, and 3D simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Compensator for Chebyshev Sharpened Comb Filter
abstract: This paper presents the design of compensators for Chebyshev sharpened CIC (cascaded-integrator-comb) decimation filters. The magnitude response of the compensator is chosen depending on the value of the passband edge of interest. The optimum compensator parameters are obtained using MATLAB particle swarm optimization (PSO). A multiplierless design is realized by presenting the optimum parameters in signed-power-of-two (SPT) forms. The method is illustrated in two examples. The proposed design is compared with the designs from the literature to show the advantages of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Electronic Components Authentication via Physical Analysis
abstract: Counterfeit electronics is a reliability problem. Undetected counterfeits can lead to increased scrap rates, early field failures, and rework rates, causing a dramatic reduction in the reliability of systems. Identifying counterfeit devices can be challenging because not everything that seems suspect is necessarily fake. On the other hand, counterfeiters keep growing and adapting.

articleTitle: A New, Reconfigurable Circuit Offering Functionality of AND and OR Logic Gates for Use in Algorithms Implemented in Hardware
abstract: The paper presents a programmable (using a 1-bit signal) digital gate that can operate in one of two OR or AND modes. A circuit of this type can also be implemented using conventional logic gates. However, in the case of the proposed circuit, compared to conventional solutions, the advantage is a much smaller number of transistors necessary for its implementation. Circuit is also much faster than its conventional counterpart. The logic gate was implemented in the 180nm CMOS technology and verified using Hspice simulations. There are many possible applications for this gate, mostly in artificial intelligence and pattern recognition algorithms implemented at the transistor level.

articleTitle: Failure Mechanisms Analysis for Integrated and Analog Position Sensors in Safety Relevant Automotive Use Cases
abstract: Modern vehicle architectures are requiring accurate positioning determination in variety of systems and system elements. Some of safety relevant examples of the position sensorics usage could include (but not be limited to) electromotor actuation, steering systems, braking & acceleration, shifting mechanisms and other systems. Connecting point of all these systems is a requirement for reliable intended functionality [1]. This aspect of reliability [2] requires careful structural top-to-bottom analysis of the possible failure mechanisms and outcomes (potential violation of safety goals [1] that may happen on a system level. This white paper will present some of the state-of-the-art Hall-effect based architectures that are available on the market, evaluate some key properties, analyze possible failure mechanisms, and propose some of the effective safety measures that may increase diagnostic coverage.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Generator for Testing the Operation of Vehicle Detection Sensors
abstract: This research paper focuses on the design of a magnetic field generator that utilizes a microcontroller, solenoid, and capacitors. The microcontroller generates a PWM signal of variable frequency and fill factor that excites the solenoid and generates a magnetic field of a different waveform. The waveforms generated for this study are sinusoidal, triangular, pulse, and one that represents the vehicle’s magnetic signature. The maximum achievable frequency with this setup is 10 Hz. The experimentally obtained results for 4 Hz waveforms confirm that the generator has satisfactory precision to generate magnetic waveforms. This type of generator has potential applications in the fields such as creating vehicle magnetic signatures and other scientific endeavors.

articleTitle: Consecutive Irradiation and Thermal Annealing of Commercial P-Channel Power VDMOSFETs
abstract: This paper presents research on the effects caused with consecutive irradiation and thermal annealing of two commercial models of p-channel power VDMOSFETs IRF9520 and IRF9530. Threshold voltage shift, which is marked as the most important parameter for both dosimetry application, as well as reliability assesment is obtained and discussed. Experiment setup, as well as the measuring procedures are explained in more detail. Irradiation degradation causes threshold voltage shift, while the thermal annealing causes recovery. The average sensitivity of models for consecutive irradiation sessions is 9.54 ± 0.04 mV Gy<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, where averagely 91.88 % is recovered through thermal annealing. Results point out that p-channel power VDMOSFET devices could be used in some dosimetry applications.

articleTitle: Modeling of Intrinsic Noise in Adsorption-Based Micro/Nanobiosensors Considering Biomolecular Rearrangement on the Sensing Surface
abstract: Sensing of biomolecules is often based on their adsorption on the sensitive surface of the sensor. Some types of biomolecules undergo changes in their spatial configuration, i.e. rearrangement, when interacting with the sensing surface. It is known that biomolecular rearrangement can significantly change the kinetics of sensor response. However, the influence of this phenomenon on sensor noise has not been investigated so far. The noise of the sensor determines its performance limits, and it can also be a source of information about the biomolecular quantity in the analyzed sample, as well as biomolecular interactions. Since the intrinsic noise originating from fluctuations of the number of the adsorbed molecules is pronounced in micro/nanobiosensors, it is useful to develop a noise model that includes all processes that affect the random change of the adsorbed amount. Such a model is essential for reliable biomolecular detection and quantification by using noise-based methods. In this paper, we present the first model of sensor intrinsic noise which, in addition to the adsorption-desorption process, also takes into account biomolecular rearrangement. Then we analyze the influence of rearrangement processes for different values of their rate constants. The obtained results show the dependence of characteristic features of the noise spectral density on the rate of conversion of adsorbed molecules from one configuration to another.

articleTitle: Efficient Neural Model of the Coplanar Inverted-F Antenna Based on MLP Networks
abstract: This research offers an EM model and a neural model based on two MultiLayer Perceptron (MLP) networks of a Coplanar Inverted F antenna. The input parameters of the neural model are ground plane length (l), height of antenna from the ground plane (h), the length of the open end (l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>) and the length of the shorter end (l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>). The realized EM model is used to generate samples that are used for training and testing the neural model. The neural model is used to quickly find the resonant frequency in range [300-3000] MHz and minimum value of the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter of a Coplanar Inverted F antenna.

articleTitle: Metal Matrix Composite Coatings Based on Ni Matrix and Biosilica Filers Obtained from Rice Husks
abstract: Electrochemically deposited nickel coatings from sulfamate baths without/with lab-made biosilica (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) particles on the Si(100) substrate were produced. Different galvanostatic regimes were used: direct current (DC), pulse current (PC), and pulse-reverse current (PRC) regimes. The phase structure of the synthesized silica nanoparticles from rice husks was obtained using XRD and FE-SEM. The MMC-Ni/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and free Ni coatings were characterized using FE-SEM, AFM, the micro indentation Vickers technique, and the drop sessile method in order to investigate structure, roughness, microhardness, and wettability. The optimal deposition parameters were obtained with an emphasis on their potential application as micro mounting coatings.

articleTitle: SPICE Modeling of Memristive Devices-Based Neural Networks
abstract: This paper reports a SPICE-based framework for circuit-level simulation of hybrid memristor/CMOS neural networks. By relying on ex-situ training, our approach systematizes the circuital representation of a neural network given a set of high-level design parameters. As a key element of simulations, we put special emphasis on the use of a recently developed compact model to represent the electrical characteristics of memristors. The model is called the Dynamic Memdiode Model (DMM) and is based on L. Chua’s theory for memristive devices. The model comprises two equations: one equation for the electron transport and one equation for the displacement of metal ions or oxygen vacancies caused by the application of the external electric field. We show how the proposed simulation framework allows to assess the influence of the circuit parasitics as well as the device non-idealities on the performance metrics of neural networks.

articleTitle: Wearable ECG Smart Patch for Mass Casualty Emergency Situations
abstract: We present a wearable ECG smart patch specifically designed for rapid cardiac monitoring in mass casualty incidents. The lightweight patch integrates three electrodes and lead-switching electronics to enable continuous heart rate measurement even with electrode detachment. An adaptive algorithm redirects ECG acquisition across alternate Lead I, II, or III configurations if any electrode disconnect is detected, using the remaining two electrodes. The smart patch system maintained the ECG analysis with only two electrodes, although signal noise increased without the right leg drive. The configurable electrode design provides constant vital sign assessment to assist rapid treatment prioritization when triaging large numbers of victims with limited resources. With further development, the wearable ECG patch has the potential to improve emergency response capacities and patient outcomes in future mass casualty situations.

articleTitle: Photothermal Pulse Response Analysis of Thin Solid Films in Time-Domain Based on Electro-Thermal Analogies
abstract: An electro-thermal analogy-based model of the pulse photothermal response of thin solid films is described in this work. Photothermally induced surface temperature variations are analogous to the model of the electric current flow through an electric network consisting of passive linear elements. The presented model is used to examine influence of thicknesses and relaxation times of thin solid films on measured photothermal signals.

articleTitle: SPICE Modeling of RADFETs with Different Gate Oxide Thicknesses
abstract: This paper will present guidelines for creating a SPICE model of RADFETs with different gate oxide thicknesses. Model parameters, such as threshold voltage and carrier mobility, were extracted from the transfer characteristics in the saturation region. The model was satisfactorily used to simulate RADFETs with oxide thicknesses ranging from 40 nm to 300 nm.

articleTitle: Memristive Multi-layer Reconfigurable Dual-Band Bandpass Filter
abstract: We propose a novel procedure for determining the novel implementation of a reconfigurable dual-band bandpass filter using planar technology. Focus is placed on the multi-layer implementation to miniaturize footprint area around 36% in relation to the single-layer realization of the same structure. The filter is realized with six coupled resonators. Filter reconfigurability is achieved using an RF memristor. There are two filter operating modes: dual-band when a memristor is in the OFF state and single band, in the other case. This filter is designed for the central frequencies of 2.467 GHz and 5.197 GHz, with the bandwidths of 145 MHz and 380 MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Temperature Effects on the Sensitivity of Gamma MOSFET Dosimeters
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between sensitivity and temperature during irradiation in MOSFET dosimeters. Three samples of the commercial lateral p-channel MOSFET 3N163 were exposed to Cobalt-60 radiation at temperatures ranging from 8 to 75 °C. Results indicate that no thermal dependence was observed up to a dose of 8 Gy.

articleTitle: Hints on Using CIC-based FIR Filters in Practice
abstract: This paper presents some hints on using new designed Cascaded-Integrator-Comb (CIC) filter functions in practice. After design the obtained filter coefficients are used in MATLAB built-in functions to filter some input signals. The filters are implemented using an efficient polyphase FIR decimation or interpolation structure.

articleTitle: A Parallel and Asynchronous Blob Shape Descriptor Implemented in CMOS Technology
abstract: The paper presents a family of novel light blob shape descriptors for use in selected active safety algorithms used in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). One of the motivations was to obtain a descriptor that would ensure low computational complexity. This makes it easy to implement both in software and hardware. One assumption is that the location of the center of a given light spot is approximately known. The principle of its operation is then to count white pixels in selected directions, starting from this central point. A key issue here is an efficient way of determining indexes of particular pixels belonging to the image patch, as well as the location of points representing places where the white area turns into black. In the case of a hardware implementation, this can be done using a parallel circuit operating in asynchronous mode, without the need for a control clock.

articleTitle: Electrical Characteristics of Chalcogenide Doped with Silver as Active Layer in Memristive Devices
abstract: Memristive and electrical properties of silver doped As-S-Se chalcogenide were investigated. Synthesis of this material was performed by melt quenching in cascade regime of heating. The structural and morphological analysis was carried out using X-ray diffraction and a scanning electron microscope. The observed multiple semicircles in recorded impedance spectra were correlated with the microstructure of the synthesized chalcogenide. Analysis of current-voltage characteristics at room temperature indicated that As-S-Se chalcogenide doped with Ag possesses good bipolar resistive switching behavior which is necessary for the fabrication of the active layer in memristive devices.

articleTitle: Resonant Nonlinear Scattering of Terahertz Waves on the Periodic System of Graphene Strips
abstract: The resonant nonlinear scattering of terahertz electromagnetic waves by the dielectric structure with a periodic system of graphene strips is investigated theoretically. The strong electron graphene nonlinearity and the electron dissipation are taken into account. The nonlinear electron dynamics is considered within the pseudo-relativistic hydrodynamic equation. The effective matrix algorithm jointly with the iteration procedure for the nonlinearity has been applied. This structure has a high quality factor. The resonant nonlinear switching of the reflection and transmission occurs in this system.

articleTitle: MgO as an Additional Layer at the Input Side of the Microchannel Plate
abstract: This paper describes one of the ways to improve the signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio of the microchannel plate. Experiments were done with MCPs with a diameter of 6µm on which a thin layer of magnesium oxide (MgO) of different thicknesses was applied to examine the influence on the electronic image and parameters of the microchannel plate.

articleTitle: Response of RADFETs to Photon Ionizing Radiation and Subsequent Recovery at Room and Elevated Temperature
abstract: The paper presents the experimental results of the response of RADFETs with an oxide thickness of 1 μm during irradiation and subsequent recovery at room and elevate temperatures. First, the results of the influence of energy of photons ionizing radiation on the threshold voltage shift for the absorbed radiation dose interval from 1 to 5 Gy are shown. It is shown that with a decrease in the energy of ionizing radiation, the value of threshold voltage shift increases and that this increase is a consequence of the increase in traps where positive charge in the oxide captured. Recovery of previously irradiated RADFETs by gamma radiation up to 5 Gy at room and elevated temperatures was also investigated. It was shown that there is no loss of dosimetric information during 20 h recovery at room temperature. Recovery at a temperature 150 °C for 500 h leads to an almost complete loss of dosimetric information, which manifests itself as the value of the threshold voltage shift being approximately equal zero. It was also shown that pre-irradiation of RADFETs up to an absorbed radiation dose of 10 mGy and recovery at room temperature leads to a significant increase in the sensitivity of these components to ionizing radiation.

articleTitle: Effects in Commercial p-Channel Power VDMOS Transistors Initiated by Negative Bias Temperature Stress and Irradiation
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of negative bias temperature stress on irradiated commercial p-channel power VDMOS transistors, particularly focusing on gate oxide charge and interface trap alterations and their contribution to threshold voltage shifts. The study addresses the critical issue of transistor reliability, as threshold voltage shifts can significantly affect device performance, especially in elevated temperature and negative gate oxide field conditions. Additionally, the research explores the effects of irradiation on VDMOS power transistors, emphasizing the importance of understanding the associated electrical parameter changes. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of static and pulsed NBT stressing, with a specific focus on novel stress signals encountered in practical applications. The experimental procedure involves irradiation and NBT stress, and the results reveal insights into the contributions of gate oxide charge and interface traps to threshold voltage shifts. The findings shed light on the reliability of electronic equipment incorporating p-channel power VDMOS transistors under various stress conditions, offering valuable insights for device design and operation.

articleTitle: Forward Bias Gate Leakage Mechanism in δ-doped β-(AlxGa1-x)2O3/Ga2O3 HFET
abstract: The forward bias gate leakage mechanisms in δ-doped β-(Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> Heterostructure Field Effect Transistor has been studied using analytical model. At higher gate voltage, when the device is turned on, the gate leakage current is prominently driven by the thermionic emission phenomenon. However, at lower gate voltage, when the device is in off state, the gate leakage is driven by the trap-assisted tunneling phenomenon. The gate leakage current model is then validated with the experimental data. The study of gate leakage mechanism is essential to ascertain the device parameter in order to minimize the gate leakage current.

articleTitle: Terahertz Nonlinear Waves and Collapsing Pulses in Hyperbolic Metamaterials Dielectric - Semiconductor
abstract: Nonlinear terahertz waves are investigated theoretically in hyperbolic metamaterials with 2 elementary layers, nonlinear dielectric and semiconductor ones. The crystalline non-polar ferroelectric SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is used as a nonlinear dielectric, the narrow-gap semiconductors like InSb, InAs are used as the second layer. In different frequency ranges the dispersion dependencies are topologically different and the frequency ranges of hyperbolicity are specified. The frequency ranges for observation of spatial solitons and collapsing pulses with wave bullets are pointed out. The wave bullets are forming under the stabilization of the collapse due to the saturation of the nonlinearity and due to the wave dissipation.

articleTitle: III-Nitride Nanowire LEDs for Enhanced Light Technology
abstract: Epitaxially grown GaN-based nanowire heterostructure arrays on (111) sapphire substrates have special characteristics and the ability to create practical devices. InGaN disks are often used as the active light-emitting device in nanowire heterostructures. By adjusting the composition of indium, the emission wavelength can be modified. In this paper, we have addressed the development of nanowire light-emitting diode for better performance in the light industry. We have designed green and yellow InGaN/AlGaN nanowire LEDs that exhibit remarkable efficiency using quantum dots grown on sapphire (111) substrate. The substrate temperature and the width of InGaN/GaN layers are the two growth parameters modified to impact the peak emission wavelengths. When compared to the results recorded at 5K, the devices exhibit comparatively higher (>40%) internal quantum efficiency at ambient temperature. A minimal blue-shift in the peak emission spectra with no efficiency droop is also observed when injection current is pushed up to 710 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Development of Smart Beehive Frame for Multi-Parameter Monitoring
abstract: Honeybees are essential for pollination in agriculture. This paper presents a smart beehive frame for multi-parameter monitoring. The system is based on opto elements that emit IR light to the honeycomb and measure the reflection. The results showed that this kind of system can be used in practice to decrease the number of the visual on-site observations of the bee colonies.

articleTitle: Electro-Acoustic Analogies Between Thermoelastic Photoacoustic Response and RC Filters
abstract: In this paper, it will be shown how to establish an electro-acoustic analogy between the transfer functions of the passive RC low-pass filter and the thermoelastic component of the photoacoustic signal. Establishing the required analogy paves the way to better thermal characterization of semiconductors, which is very important for the correct functioning of many electronic components individually, or as part of micro- or nano-electromechanical structures. To confirm this analogy, the experimental results will be shown, which were performed on an aluminum sample.

articleTitle: X-band Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Based on Lithium-Niobium-Titanium-Oxide Microwave Ceramics
abstract: In this study, we report on the performance of the cylindrical dielectric resonator fabricated by lithium-niobium-titanium-oxide (LNTO) ceramics modified with 0 and 5 wt% of ZnO as functional additive. These microwave ceramic materials were prepared by using a combustion-assisted solid-state reaction method and final cylindrical pellets with diameter of 9.5 mm and height of 1.3 mm were sintered at 900°C for 4 h. Using scanning electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction techniques, structural analysis confirmed the densely packed structure of the synthesized M-phase type LNTO ceramics with an average crystallite size in the nano range. The LNTO sample with 5 wt% of ZnO showed a higher temperature stability of dielectric constant and resonant frequency compared to the LNTO sample without ZnO. Further, the fabricated LNTO ceramic-based dielectric resonator possesses the minimum of the return loss at resonant frequency of 9.85 GHz with relative bandwidth of 4.9%.

articleTitle: Simulation of Helmholtz and Maxwell Coils using FEMM 4.2
abstract: Simulation of Helmholtz and Maxwell coils is performed in this paper using software FEMM 4.2. The obtained results have been compared with analytical solutions, as well as with the results obtained using QuickField software. The values for magnetic flux density in different points of the systems are presented in tables and graphically.

articleTitle: Optical Glasses Transmittance Reduction Under Gamma Radiation Exposure at Different Temperatures
abstract: The paper discusses the results of a study on the changes in transmittance coefficient of optical glasses at wavelengths of 455, 808, and 1550 nm under gamma radiation exposure up to a total accumulated dose of 2 Mrad at ambient temperatures of +25 °C and -30 °C are presented. The purpose of the study was a qualitative comparison of the radiation resistance of typical representatives of the classes of optical glasses: lanthanum crown, heavy flint, crown and heavy lanthanum flint.

articleTitle: Is Microelectronics Recognizable in Serbian School System?
abstract: This paper presents the results of multi-year activities with high school students and faculty students in the field of practical application of electronic devices. A special review is given to the Arduino courses that have been organized at the Faculty of Electronic Engineering Niš in the past 6 years. In addition to the organization of courses, the authors also conducted numerous surveys to examine the impact of practical work on the progress of students during the studies at the faculty. The ultimate goal is the correction of the curriculum in high schools and/or technical faculties.

articleTitle: Influence of Grain Growth on Electric Properties of Er-Doped BaTiO3
abstract: This paper investigated the effect of grain growth on the electrical characteristics of Er-doped BaTiO3 ceramics. The concentrations of Er2O3 ranged from 0.01 to 1.0 at% Er. For the samples doped with a low concentration of additives and sintered at 1320°C, a uniform microstructure with an average grain size of 1 - 5 °m is characteristic. In Er-BaTiO3 ceramics sintered at a higher temperature, in samples doped with a higher concentration of dopants, the appearance of secondary abnormal grains with a domain structure was observed. Higher values of the dielectric constant were obtained for samples with a lower concentration of dopants (0.01 and 0.1 at% Er) sintered at 1380°C. For samples with an Er content above 0.5 at%, the lower value of the dielectric constant is due to secondary abnormal grain growth and the presence of a non-ferroelectric phase rich in Er. Very low values of dielectric losses (from 0.006 to 0.02) are characteristic of all tested samples. Electrical resistivity decreases with increasing additive concentration up to 0.5 at%, while it increases above 0.5 at% of Er.

articleTitle: Short-term Recovery Effect in a Power Integrated Circuit Exposed to X-Rays
abstract: During the previous examinations of a negative voltage regulator in various bremsstrahlung fields, a short-term recovery effect was perceived in some samples. In one set of bias and load conditions of the examined power integrated circuit, it was observed that the usual trend of (the absolute value of) the output voltage decline, perceived in all the other samples, was briefly violated. Thus, a slight recovery of the output voltage during irradiation was observed, followed by another drop in the output voltage, until the circuit shuts down. In the research presented, an effort has been made to model this effect using the previously developed SPICE micromodel of LM2990T-5.0 circuit. Radiation induced leakage currents have been simulated in critical transistors in the operational amplifier circuit, recreating the conditions prior to device failure after X-ray exposure.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Graphene for Wearable Respiratory Monitoring
abstract: Laser-induced graphene (LIG) shows promise as an active sensing material for a wearable respiratory monitoring system. This work describes the integration of a graphene-based sensor and an electronic system for real-time respiratory monitoring. The sensor transduces body movements during breathing into resistance changes after which the resistance is converted into a digital signal using the developed electronic system. An adjustable current source provides optimal biasing based on microcontroller calibration. Measurements on a supine subject exhibit good waveforms corresponding to breathing cycles. While signal filtering is needed to improve the signal-to-noise ratio, the capability of laser-induced graphene for respiratory monitoring is demonstrated. With optimization of material synthesis and electronics, the laser-induced graphene sensing concept could enable non-invasive respiration monitoring for advanced healthcare applications. The further development of wireless connectivity, data storage, user interfaces, and algorithmic processing could allow the practical deployment of this technology for diagnostic applications.

articleTitle: Photoinduced Currents (Nanoamperes) at Single Crystalline Cadmium Telluride Surfaces Analyzed at Ambient by Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
abstract: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) is being employed to study photoexcited charged carriers at semiconductors surfaces. However, so far, the investigation was limited to relatively low resistivity materials, and the experimental setup was placed within an Ultra High Vacuum (UHV) chamber. In the current research, we were able to carry out photo assisted STM analysis at ambient on well-determined cadmium telluride single crystalline surfaces with high resistivity of about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> Ω•cm, oriented to the (111) Cd, (111) Te and (110) cleaved surface. The recorded data was found to be in good agreement with the published results that were achieved by surface photo-voltage spectroscopy. Such information may be useful as an effective characterization method for materials prior to the fabrication of wide band-gap semiconductor detectors.

articleTitle: Breakdown Voltage Stability Testing of Gas Surge Arrester Littelfuse CG2300 Under Different Environmental Conditions
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of voltage stability and breakdown characteristics of gas surge arrester under the influence of ionizing radiation. The study involves testing 20 identical gas components. The gas surge arresters were subjected to different voltage increase rates. Experimental results revealed three distinct breakdown voltage groups. This study provides insights into the effects of radiation on gas surge arrester behavior, offering valuable information for applications in diverse fields.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Microporous Ceramic Heatsinks in Thermal Energy Harvesting Systems
abstract: The microporous ceramic heatsinks are suitable for heat dissipation in systems where natural cooling prevails within a limited space. This paper investigates the effectiveness of low- profile microporous ceramic heatsinks in conjunction with thermoelectric generators for powering the wireless sensor network nodes in natural cooling conditions. The minimum temperature differences between the heat source and the ambient necessary for the node's continuous operation are in the range of 18 °C to 29 °C, with delivered power of about 0.5 mW.

articleTitle: A Monotonic Asynchronous Full Adder
abstract: This paper presents a new input-output mode asynchronous full adder that is monotonic and early output type. In a monotonic asynchronous circuit, the intermediate outputs and primary outputs experience similar signal transitions as the primary inputs for the application of data and/or spacer. The proposed full adder exhibits monotonicity for processing data and spacer. The full adder employs dual-rail encoding for inputs and outputs and corresponds to return-to-zero handshaking. The early output nature of the proposed full adder could facilitate the production of sum and carry outputs based on the adder inputs without having to wait for the carry input when the spacer is supplied. When incorporated in a ripple carry adder (RCA) structure, the proposed full adder enables reductions in all the design metrics viz. cycle time, area, and total power dissipation compared to existing gate-level asynchronous full adders. Compared to the best of the existing high-speed asynchronous full adders, the proposed full adder enables a 10.4% reduction in cycle time and a 15.8% reduction in area without any power penalty when incorporated in a 32-bit RCA, for implementation using a 28-nm CMOS technology. In terms of power-cycle time product, which is representative of energy, the proposed full adder enables an 11.8% reduction.

articleTitle: Open Innovation Strategies in Engineering Education
abstract: This article considers two approaches to improving engineering education through open innovation: one focuses on informal educational activities through organizing student competitions and hackathons, and the second focuses on implementing project-based learning in formal education. The main goal is to compare the effectiveness and implementation challenges of the two proposed strategies. Both approaches were implemented at the University of Belgrade, Faculty of Organizational Sciences, for teaching and learning the subjects in IT education, namely blockchain technologies and IoT. The results show that both approaches provide good results and positively affect learning outcomes and students' motivation. We analyze the advantages and challenges of each of them in detail and provide guidelines for their implementation.

articleTitle: Resiliency in Digital Processing Systems
abstract: Reliability in integrated circuits (ICs) has been an important topic for many years. Numerous methods for achieving reliability in ICs have been proposed. Nevertheless, the traditional approaches come with significant overhead and are not optimal for complex dynamic digital systems, which we have today. Today’s systems should be resilient - they need to dynamically react to intrinsic and environmental changes, and ideally be able to predict the possible threats even before they appear. This paper provides an overview on how to approach the resiliency in digital processing systems. The resilient approach is demonstrated in a fabricated IC based on RISC-V architecture, supporting on-chip fault sensing and dynamic system adaptation.

articleTitle: Recent Applications of Polylogarithms in MOSFET Modeling
abstract: We present a review of recent uses of the special mathematical function known as the polylogarithm for MOSFET modeling applications. We first summarize some basic properties of polylogarithms, with a particular focus on those with negative exponential argument. After examining cases of the use of first order polylogarithms pertinent to electron device modeling, we explain the reasons that motivate the use of polylogarithms of diverse orders for formulating mono- and poly-crystalline succinct compact MOSFET models. We then analyze a particular representative example: the modeling of polysilicon MOSFETs using the polylogarithm. Recalling that polylogarithms may be used to faithfully represent Fermi-Dirac Integrals in general, and considering that they are analytically differentiable and integrable, we describe a fully Fermi–Dirac Statistics-based version of the usually approximate Boltzmann Statistics-based MOSFET Surface Potential Equation (SPE).

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Spam Detection in Social Media Feeds
abstract: Twitter, Facebook, and Reddit are popular social networking sites for online interaction. These platforms use spam filtering techniques to identify and block spammers. However, discovering spammers is challenging in Online Social Networks (OSNs). The most commonly used technique to identify spammers is classification-based supervised techniques. However, these sys- tems are subject to "data manipulation," "imbalanced datasets," "data marking," and "spam flow" restrictions. Malicious users exploit implicit trust ties between users to spread false infor- mation, post or tweet malicious websites, and contact legitimate people without their consent. Using unlabeled URLs in a semi- supervised manner and synthetic harmful URLs produced via adversarial learning can reduce the need for labelled samples and solve the imbalance problem. The characteristics of spam users on Twitter are investigated to enhance the effectiveness of current spam detection systems. A collection of new features, more reliable and effective than previously used ones, are used to identify Twitter spammers. The suggested attributes are evaluated using well-known machine learning classification algorithms, such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), several Naive Bayesian (NB) methods, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Random Forest (RF).

articleTitle: Classifier Fusion Based on Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) in the Function of Classification Emotional Speech, Using Spectral and Prosodic Features
abstract: Various types of information are imprinted in the speech signal, which the interlocutor registers with his auditory perceptual system. The number of transmitted messages, hidden in the speech signal, is numerous, because they give a stamp on the complete personality of the speaker: his biological, sociological, psychological and social dimensions. Studying and analyzing the emotional characteristics of the speech signal requires knowledge of several scientific fields, such as information technology, psychology, pedagogy, acoustics, signal processing, linguistics, medicine, artificial intelligence and many others. In the process of processing human speech, in order to determine the emotional state of the speaker, in this paper we used its spectral and prosodic characteristics. As the emotional state of the speaker causes a change in the vocal tract in relation to neutral speech, a change in rhythm, intonation, melodicity, volume and other changes, i.e. adequate changes in the spectral plane, we believe that these characteristics are relevant in the speech signal for determining the emotional state of the speaker. Also, prosodic characteristics related to rhythm, accent, intensity and intonation of speech [3] largely reflect emotional speech. In order to classify the speech signal into a specific emotional group, a fusion of classifiers based on Gaussian Mixture Model was used (GMM) and Support vector machine (SVM). SAVEE emotional speech database was used for training and testing data.

articleTitle: Application of Charge Pumping Technique for MOSFET Devices Reliability
abstract: In this paper, we present an overview of charge-pumping technique (CPT) and its applications in field-effect transistors (FET) reliability during couple of decades, giving insight into its potentialities. We describe the evolution of CPT, starting from the most popular one "conventional CPT" and follow up with its different variants to study uniform and non-uniform degradations in FET devices fabricated with old and advanced semiconductor and dielectric materials. In addition, we illustrate its ability to characterize transistors with specific geometries. Its limitations and solutions are also discussed.
